components.rationale: Lines 14-20 fix the structure class: a finite, purely relational signature tau whose relation symbols all have positive arity, with no constant or function symbols; a labeled n-element tau-structure has universe [n]={0,...,n-1}. They also fix the probability model: uniform distribution over all such labeled structures. The text states that these restrictions are part of the zero-one law. Lines 25-27 repeat the model inside the theorem: A_n is uniformly random among the labeled tau-structures on [n]. Lines 39-40 explicitly exclude constants and function symbols, which would need a separately specified space. The G(n,1/2) switch at lines 42-47 is announced as applying to that paragraph only. The structure and probability model of the chosen labeled-uniform law are therefore plainly specified.

For every first-order tau-sentence phi, with A_n uniform over labeled tau-structures on [n], it states that lim Pr[A_n |= phi] exists and lies in {0,1}. It is Fagin's word a#b_1#...#b_r over {0,1,#}, with a = n in binary and b_i the lexicographic characteristic string of length n^{m_i}. It also defines E(A), the shift from [n], order-insensitivity under isomorphism closure, and the announced exclusion of empty tau (Fagin's Theorem 6(2), NP_1).
